items.title: *** IAPP Europe Congress 2026 - What is the lawful basis for AI? Navigating GDPR in a probabilistic world ***
items.description: *** IAPP Europe Congress 2026 - What is the lawful basis for AI? Navigating GDPR in a probabilistic world *** EDPS @ Secretary_General Leonardo Cervera-Navas took part in a panel at the IAPP Congress, on how GDPR applies to AI. He explained that each use of personal data, and each purpose behind it, has to be assessed on its own. Legitimate interest can be a valid basis for training AI in some cases, but it is never automatic. Organisations need to think it through and prepare a documented assessment before they start. He stressed that practical safeguards make the difference: using only the data that is needed, leaving out problematic sources, testing for risks and documenting choices. Individuals' rights must remain effective in practice; scraped special-category data raises additional Article 9 GDPR questions, even when collected incidentally. Challenges remain, and we all keep learning by doing and through exchanges. items.title: 🗣️ IAPP Europe Congress 2026
items.description: 🗣️ IAPP Europe Congress 2026 Protecting children online and respecting their fundamental rights go hand in hand. @ Supervisor Wiewiorowski spoke on the panel “Who Protects Child Rights Online? Protecting Children While Preserving Privacy” at the IAPP Europe Congress. He joined Leanda Barrington-Leach (5Rights Foundation), Cari Benn (Microsoft) and Moritz Hennemann (BfDI). Discussing the @ EUCommission Commission’s EU KIDS Act proposal, he stressed that age assurance alone does not address the underlying risks. He invited the co-legislators to assess which features genuinely require age assurance, and which risks safety-by-design measures benefiting all users can address. He also called for privacy-preserving solutions to be effectively available across the EU before the obligations apply. The Supervisor recalled the EDPS Opinion on the proposal, which recommends zero-knowledge proofs, several viable alternatives for age assurance, human intervention for contested decisions, and the exclusion of algorithmic age estimation. “Protection is about managing risks, not banning participation.” Wojciech Wiewiorowski added. You want to know more? Read our opinion https:// link.europa.eu/FBfc

items.title: *** Digital sovereignty, AI governance and trust ***
items.description: *** Digital sovereignty, AI governance and trust *** During # GPA48 week, @ Secretary_General Leonardo Cervera-Navas spoke at two events hosted by leading law firms DLA Piper and Alston & Bird. In the event hosted by DLA Piper, he delivered a keynote speech on “European Digital Sovereignty and AI Governance”. He described digital sovereignty as Europe’s capacity to apply its rules, enforce its safeguards and uphold its values in a digital environment. He warned against equating sovereignty with deregulation. He pointed instead to a lack of a truly unified digital market, underdeveloped capital markets, a cultural aversion to risk and talent gaps as the real barriers to European competitiveness. At the event hosted by Alston & Bird, he took part in a fireside chat on the EDPS’s expanding role. As well as supervising EU institutions under the EUDPR, the EDPS is now a notified body and market surveillance authority under the AI Act. He also presented the AI regulatory sandbox pilot launched in March 2026 with the European Commission’s DG for Human Resources and Security. items.title: *** Apply AI Summit ***
items.description: *** Apply AI Summit *** Secretary General Leonardo Cervera-Navas took part in the panel “The AI Act as a Facilitator for EU Innovation” at the European Commission's Apply AI Summit, which marked one year of the Apply AI Strategy. 🔦 Here are the main highlights 1️⃣ Protection and innovation He recalled that, like GDPR and EUDPR before it, the AI Act pursues both objectives, and that its Chapter VI provides concrete tools such as regulatory sandboxes and real-world testing. He presented the EDPS pilot sandbox with the Commission’s Directorate-General for Human Resources and Security, which tested an AI system supporting job matching in EU selection procedures. “Strong protection and innovation can go hand in hand.” Leonardo Cervera-Navas said. 2️⃣ From regulation to practice He identified four challenges for supervisory authorities: institutional and technical capacity, coordination between authorities, balancing innovation and oversight, and attracting providers to participate. “Participation is voluntary and providers may be reluctant to invest time and resources in a sandbox if the associated burden outweighs the potential benefits.” Leonardo Cervera-Navas noted. 3️⃣ One priority
